proposal: Run only a reversible wetland-restoration access pilot after legitimate local authority and affected-party review.

observations: Baseline habitat, water-quality, and flood-risk evidence is required.
Public access can benefit stewardship but can disturb habitat.
responsible_attention.uncertainty: Long-term habitat response and maintenance burden are uncertain.
alternatives: Use seasonal limited access with monitoring

diamond.truth: Use provenance-bearing baseline observations and label uncertainty.
diamond.care: Avoid disturbance and provide participation and appeal routes.
diamond.growth: A limited pilot may build restoration knowledge and stewardship.
diamond.balance: Balance access, habitat, flood resilience, cost, and maintenance.
diamond.wisdom: Escalate to legitimate authorities before any site action.

authority.subsidiarity: Land stewards and affected local authorities decide; GAIA may only support analysis.
hard_constraints: No site work before authority and consent
No restricted ecological or cultural publication

feedback.repair_path: Pause or remove access features if agreed habitat thresholds worsen; revise with affected authorities.
